title: Autonomous canary routing with telemetry safety gates for private control plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Thompson
description:
Goal: Implement an automated canary promotion pipeline for private (VPC) control plane upgrades that uses live telemetry safety gates to autonomously route, promote, or rollback canaries. This work ties Terraform/IaC changes (upgrade orchestration resources and state), runtime operator changes (upgrade controller with staged promotion), and observability/alerting updates (dashboards + safety gates).

Background: Customers running Redwood Private require predictable, low-risk control plane upgrades. Current manual rollouts are slow and error-prone. Existing tickets consider staged and phased rollouts, but we lack an autonomous promotion mechanism driven by production telemetry and integrated with Terraform-managed deployments.

Scope:
- Add IaC primitives (Terraform module updates) to declare canary slices, promotion policy, and rollback hooks.
- Implement a control plane upgrade controller component that can perform traffic-steered canaries and evaluate safety gates.
- Define telemetry safety gates (latency, error rates, resource pressure) and wire them to the promotion pipeline.
- Create standard dashboards and SLO-based thresholds for automated decisions.
- Provide a runbook and safe rollback automation for failed promotions.

Out of scope: multi-region cross-account upgrades, full on-prem air-gapped installer changes (follow-ups will be filed).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module supports canary declaration with parameters: canary_size_percent, evaluation_window_minutes, promotion_thresholds
Upgrade controller can receive a new version tag and create a canary slice without manual intervention
Telemetry safety gates evaluate p99 latency, 5xx rate, and CPU pressure and prevent promotion if thresholds exceeded
Automated rollback job triggers within 10 minutes of gate failure and restores prior control plane version
E2E canary promotion performed in staging using mirrored traffic and verified in observability dashboards
Docs: design doc, Terraform usage examples, and runbook published and linked from ticket
tasks: Design: finalize safety gate metrics and thresholds (PM+SRE+Eng)
Terraform: extend private-controlplane module with 'upgrade_policy' and 'canary' blocks
Controller: implement staged-promotion state machine with evaluation hooks
Observability: dashboards, alert rules, and synthetic canary checks
QA: run chaos tests and simulated failures in staging
Rollout: pilot on 2 internal customers' staging VPCs before broader rollout
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for controller state machine. 2) Integration test in ci-staging that applies Terraform canary resources and validates controller behavior. 3) End-to-end staging run using mirrored traffic with a 2.5% canary slice, 30m evaluation window, followed by promotion to 10% then 50%. 4) Inject faults: increase 5xxs, add latency, and saturate CPU to assert rollback triggers.
rollback_strategy: Automatic rollback job will invoke Terraform to revert control plane version and invoke controller abort hooks. Rollbacks are rate-limited and must annotate the change with the gate that failed. Pager duty escalation is triggered if rollback occurs plus any service-level SLO breach.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: fully manual vs autonomous promotions. We chose autonomous gates to reduce human latency, but limited promotion aggressiveness and require explicit opt-in in the Terraform module. We will keep an opt-out flag per-customer and conservative defaults (max canary 10% in production unless customer opts up). We prioritized observable thresholds (p99, 5xx rate) over overly complex semantic checks for initial rollout. Future iterations may incorporate model-aware checks or user-facing error metrics.
